name: New Hampshire

agency.name: New Hampshire Department of Labor, Workers' Compensation Division

ttd.rateText: 60% of the employee's gross average weekly wage, or 30% of the state average weekly wage if greater, never more than 150% of the SAWW and never more than 100% of the employee's after-tax weekly earnings (RSA 281-A:28, II); an employee earning 30% of SAWW or less receives full wages, capped at 90% of after-tax earnings (RSA 281-A:28, I).
ttd.minText: Minimum = 30% of SAWW, or the full average weekly wage if lower, never above 90% of after-tax earnings (RSA 281-A:28, I-II).
ttd.periodLabel: injuries July 1, 2025 - June 30, 2026 (latest period published by NH DOL as of 2026-10-08)

waiting.text: No compensation for the first 3 days of disability unless the disability continues for 14 days or longer (RSA 281-A:28). The waiting period is also waived if the worker returns to temporary alternative duty within 5 days of the injury (RSA 281-A:23-b, NH DOL).

ttdDuration.text: TTD is paid while the employee is totally disabled and has not reached maximum medical improvement; no fixed week cap in RSA 281-A:28. Temporary partial benefits are limited to 262 weeks for injuries on or after 2/8/94, less weeks of total disability paid (NH DOL).

ppd.text: Permanent impairment awards (RSA 281-A:32) are a single payment: percentage of loss (AMA Guides 5th edition) x the statutory number of weeks for the body part (e.g. arm 210 weeks; whole person 350 weeks) x the compensation rate. Paid in addition to weekly compensation once the worker is at a medical endpoint (NH DOL).

facts.text: New Hampshire's maximum (150% of SAWW, $2,309.00 from July 1, 2025) is among the highest in the US, but every rate is also capped at 100% of the worker's after-tax earnings (RSA 281-A:28; NH DOL rate table).
Average weekly wage uses the 26 weeks before the injury, but the worker may ask to use anywhere from 26 to 52 weeks, whichever is most beneficial (NH DOL).
Employers with 5 or more employees must develop temporary alternative work, and must reinstate an injured employee to the former position within 18 months (RSA 281-A:23-b, 281-A:25-a; NH DOL).
Carriers have 30 days to pay or deny a medical bill; failure can bring a fine of up to $2,500 (NH DOL).
Workers concurrently employed by two or more NH-covered employers receive benefits based on combined earnings (NH DOL).

uncertain: 2026 value not published by NH Department of Labor as of 2026-10-08; latest official = July 1, 2025 ($2,309.00 max / $461.74 min) from the rate table revised June 9, 2025. NH resets rates each July 1, so a July 1, 2026 figure probably exists but was not found on dol.nh.gov or mm.nh.gov.
